source_observation.not_claimed: No exploit, state mutation, runtime promotion or downstream semantic consumption of an unknown field has been demonstrated.

hypothesis.claim: Promotion-bearing authority envelopes should reject unknown top-level fields rather than preserve fields outside the authority identity commitment, preventing later schema extension or downstream consumers from accidentally assigning semantics to uncommitted data.
hypothesis.counterhypothesis: If every downstream consumer forever ignores unknown fields and an outer proof envelope commits the complete object, the current behavior may be non-exploitable at present.
hypothesis.adjudication: The counterhypothesis does not remove the fail-closed maintenance risk. Closed authority schemas make the semantic commitment boundary explicit and prevent future consumers from silently turning previously ignored data into authority-bearing meaning.
hypothesis.falsifier: Show an exact-current closed-field-set guard before authority-envelope acceptance, or prove by a stronger typed boundary that unknown fields cannot survive into any promotion-bearing consumer.

external_method_research.use_in_clay: Supports a future model-specific diagnostic after exact Qwen3.5 runtime authorization; it does not justify copying the reported layers/heads or creating positive J-Space labels now.

external_method_research.source: Wu, Geiger, Milliere, ICML 2025, How Do Transformers Learn Variable Binding in Symbolic Programs?
external_method_research.source_claim: A trained Transformer learned systematic variable binding after a heuristic phase; causal interventions implicated residual-stream addressable memory and specialized routing heads in the studied model.
